rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-four builder trees go (a row of corals, torrey pines and queen palms every 6-16 m along the back fences, a fan palm 3 m from a house front, magnolias and others in the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the adirondack chairs, the beach umbrella, on the open lot corner, and two in back yards 7.5-8 m from the houses.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m west, 12 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the open lot corner to the north, 16.5 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the east back yard with the two white adirondack chairs: shade for them
the yard by the closed beach umbrella: a coral tree over the lounging spot
the south back yard, 7.5 m from the house: the yard's tree
the south-west back yard, 8 m from the house, 32 m from the next
